outcomes.text: Recognize French sounds, words, basic phrases, and clear simple instructions, then repeat or respond appropriately.
Recognize familiar everyday words and signs when spoken or presented clearly and slowly in familiar situations.
Understand personal information and follow brief conversations about nationality, family, routines, hobbies, and similar topics.
Understand sequences of instructions for familiar activities, including sports, cooking, and making bookings.
Introduce yourself and exchange questions and answers about personal information, residence, acquaintances, and possessions.
Use common French greetings and farewells, and ask or give simple information about people and places.
Identify or redirect a slowly spoken conversation topic, and ask or answer questions about personal information and daily life.
Use simple verbal and non-verbal signals to show interest and understand predictable information in brief signs, notices, posters, and programmes.
Produce brief phrases about personal details, preferences, likes, and dislikes.
Recognize familiar words and signs supported by pictures, using familiar vocabulary, and distinguish different sounds.
Identify familiar names, words, and basic phrases in short, simple texts.
Infer unfamiliar words or signs from familiar texts and read basic words and phrases in short passages.
Read short, simple texts containing everyday, employment-related, or internationally shared vocabulary.
Find and understand essential information in advertisements, leaflets, and brochures.
Identify an article, book, or chapter title and understand captions and subheadings.
Recognize and use French salutations, greetings, and farewells.
Recognize the French alphabet.
Discuss personal information, including name, address, and age.
Recognize cardinal numbers.
Recognize and use ordinal numbers.
Recognize the days of the week and the months.
Use vocabulary for body parts, including hands, feet, and head.
Identify and pronounce country names and nationalities accurately.
Use classroom vocabulary, including objects and people found in a classroom.
Identify and recall basic colour names such as black, white, and red.
Tell the time using hours, minutes, and seconds.
Identify and discuss family members and relationships.
Talk about food and drink.
Develop basic words and phrases for particular concrete situations.
Recognise and name common household furniture, including beds, chairs, tables, and sofas.
Recognise and name various hobbies and sporting activities.
Describe city locations such as hospitals, railway stations, and restaurants.
Discuss vocabulary connected with weather.
Describe clothing items such as shirts, trousers, and shoes.
Explain different means of transport, including buses, cars, and trains.
Distinguish common adjectives such as small, tall, and beautiful.
Identify common animals, including cats, dogs, and birds.
Express basic emotions such as happiness, sadness, and tiredness.
Name common jobs and professions.
Recognize and use food-related vocabulary when ordering in a restaurant.
Recognize and use shopping vocabulary, including stores, money, and prices.
Identify and use travel vocabulary such as tickets, suitcases, and hotels.
Describe everyday routines, including waking, washing, and going to bed.
Recognize and name vocabulary connected with nature and the environment.
Recognize and name technology-related vocabulary, including computers, phones, and the internet.
Recognise and name vocabulary related to technology, including computers, phones, and the internet.
Identify and use vocabulary for describing physical appearance, including height and body size.
Recognize and use common everyday expressions, nouns, and adjectives.
Recognize and use the verbs être and avoir.
Identify and use personal pronouns: je, tu, il or elle, nous, vous, and ils or elles.
Use definite articles le, la, and les, and indefinite articles un, une, and des.
Recognize conjugation rules for regular first-group -er verbs such as parler and habiter.
Apply correct usage rules for adjectives and nouns.
Recognize and use negation with ne…pas.
Construct irregular and semi-irregular -er verbs, including aller, appeler, and jeter.
Distinguish and correctly use oui, non, and si.
Recognize and conjugate regular and irregular -re verbs, including prendre, rendre, apprendre, and dire.
Recognize and use place prepositions such as à, en, au, and aux.
Recognize and conjugate regular and irregular -ir verbs, including finir, choisir, voir, and devoir.
Use the near-future and recent-past tenses.
Use reflexive verbs correctly.
Distinguish countable from uncountable nouns and use the partitive articles du, de la, and des.
Use demonstrative adjectives ce, cet, cette, ces and possessive adjectives mon, ma, mes correctly.
Use the place prepositions dans, chez, sur and sous appropriately.
Use interrogative expressions such as qu’est-ce que, est-ce que and quand.
Use French phonetic sounds consistently to form words accurately.
Spell and write both familiar and unfamiliar words accurately.
Use punctuation marks correctly, including periods, commas, and question marks.
Conjugate verbs and spell words correctly by recognizing silent endings.
Write simple phrases and complete forms or questionnaires with personal information.
Write brief informal messages or letters describing vacations, celebrations, and activities.
Compose short messages and online posts expressing preferences, likes, and dislikes in the present tense.
Use simple language to describe everyday objects, including their colour, size, and appearance.
Identify and name familiar expressions describing feelings, such as happiness, sadness, and surprise, along with basic everyday phrases.
Use numbers, prices, and dates appropriately in familiar everyday situations.
Understand key details in short recordings or broadcasts about everyday subjects, such as weather forecasts, sports, and results.
Recognize numbers, prices, and times in announcements at places such as railway stations, airports, and shops.
Participate successfully in conversations with other people.
Exchange information directly and simply while completing familiar routine tasks.
Understand announcements about events and transport, such as cinema schedules, sports fixtures, and train or plane delays.
Give and understand short, simple answers using correct syntax, pronunciation, and appropriate present, past, and future tenses.
Exchange information about familiar, routine matters through simple and direct communication.
Explain the meanings of unfamiliar words by using their surrounding context.
Answer short questions and multiple-choice questions about illustrated narratives.
Extract information from texts and present it through matching, linking, ordering, or copying activities.
Respond to texts containing everyday, employment-related, or internationally shared vocabulary.
Find particular information in lists, texts, leaflets, and notices, then respond appropriately.
Begin reading short, simple stories and comic strips about familiar concrete situations using common everyday language.
Understand main points in short magazine reports or guide entries about concrete everyday subjects.
Describe seasons and weather conditions.
Use vocabulary concerning the environment, weather, and seasons.
Recognize vocabulary for food items.
Name common utensils.
Discuss vocabulary associated with money.
Discuss city life and related activities.
Discuss various academic subjects and studies.
Practice vocabulary connected with health and the body.
Explore historical, social, and linguistic dimensions of countries and nationalities.
Discuss familiar topics such as home country, family, and school using appropriate vocabulary.
Join conversations on familiar topics, express opinions, and exchange everyday information.
Use enough vocabulary and circumlocution to discuss everyday topics such as family, hobbies, work, and travel.
Read brief, straightforward texts containing frequently used vocabulary.
Write diary entries about routines, activities, people, and places using simple vocabulary, sentences, and connectors.
Write personal impressions and opinions about familiar interests, lifestyles, culture, and stories.
Translate very short, familiar everyday texts into the target language using simple, understandable language.
Use suitable vocabulary to manage everyday tasks and interactions in familiar situations.
Use suitable vocabulary to communicate basic needs.
Use a broad vocabulary range when discussing familiar subjects and everyday situations.
Use elementary vocabulary effectively, while recognizing that complex ideas and unfamiliar situations may produce errors.
Use a broad selection of simple vocabulary appropriately for familiar subjects.
Understand familiar words and expressions when speech about personal topics is slow and clear.
Write simple information about personally relevant matters using basic words and expressions.
Distinguish adjectives from adverbs and apply their inflections correctly.
Determine meanings of unfamiliar or multiple-meaning words using flexible strategies.
Use surrounding sentence, paragraph, or text context to infer word and phrase meanings.
Identify word-form patterns that signal changes in meaning or grammatical category.
Identify word changes that signal different meanings or grammatical categories, such as analyse, analysis, and analytical.
Use reference sources, in print or digital form, to check pronunciation, meaning, grammatical category, or word origin.
Recognize and correctly use the relative pronouns qui, que, and où.
Form and use the passé composé in affirmative and negative sentences.
Use pour and afin de appropriately in writing.
Identify and use direct object pronouns appropriately.
Use indefinite determiners such as aucun and plusieurs.
Form nouns from verbs and adjectives through nominalization.
Recognize and use negation with ne…plus and ne…jamais.
Use restriction with ne…que and seulement in sentences.
Form sentences containing dative and accusative objects together, using forms such as moi, toi, and soi.
Use adverbs of frequency appropriately.
Recognize and use place prepositions such as à côté de and en face de.
Recognize, identify, and use affirmative imperative forms such as fermez, entrez, and ouvrez.
Form and use the imperfect tense in affirmative and negative sentences.
Use reflexive verbs in the past tense.
Use comparative and superlative forms.
Form and use the simple future tense.
Recognize and correctly use the direct-object pronouns le, la and les.
Recognize and appropriately use lequel and laquelle in writing.
Use a systematic method to check and confirm correct word spelling.
Apply gender and singular-to-plural rules when writing French nouns in sentences.
Write accurately and fluently on varied subjects using appropriate grammar and organization.
Conjugate verbs in different tenses and maintain gender and number agreement.
Link simple phrases and sentences with connectors such as “et,” “mais,” and “parce que.”
Write simple formal or informal letters, or report problems concerning immediate needs.
Write varied familiar texts, such as diary entries, story openings, introductions, and event descriptions.
Write simple texts describing events, activities, and experiences using present and past information.
